messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Continuous-batching service 'cb-router' high tail latency > 2s for 95th% over last 3m. Alarm: cb.p95.latency > 2s (region: us-west-2). Affected: hosted API tier.
sam (oncall): acknowledging — investigating. starting with KV cache and batching metrics.
liam (sre): I see a sharp increase in inflight queue size across many pods ~ 00:10 UTC, also microbatch sizes collapsed to 1-2 often. likely jitter causing batch inefficiency.
tess (eng-runtime): thanks. can you paste the logs for prefetch and kv-eviction spikes? suspecting cache blowups from prefetch churn.
liam (sre): pasting short snippet from pod cb-router-7f6b: ```[00:09:58] prefetch: keys=124k p95=1.8ms; evict-triggered=true; kv_cache_size=98%
[00:10:02] batch: microbatch_size=1 inflight=512 queue_depth=700
[00:10:04] latency: token_p95=2103ms token_p99=4500ms```
sam (oncall): ok that matches symptom set we've seen with continuous-batch->kv regen loops. initial mitigation options: reduce prefetch aggressiveness = fastest, fallback -> disable continuous batching on 20% of traffic for canary, or increase microbatch target to force coalescing.
tess (eng-runtime): hotfix candidate: flip config flag prefetch.max_concurrency from 64 -> 16 and kv.prefetch_throttle=true. We can roll to single region and observe.
liam (sre): agree. also good to open a temporary rate-limit on new streaming sessions to stop the influx. nina can we do customer impact assessment?
nina (prod-ops): pulling customer top-level metrics. initial glance: ~1.3% of hosted requests are seeing p95>2s, but that surfaces for 20 customers with high concurrency. only 2 customers report errors (timeouts), others are latency-only. marking possible SLA exposure for pay-as-you-go.
alina (support): i've flagged the 2 customers and opened support tickets; customers notified of degraded performance, we promised follow-up in 30m.
sam (oncall): action plan: (1) roll prefetch throttle hotfix to cb-router pool A (10% of pods) now, (2) enable microbatch floor to 8 tokens on affected machines, (3) apply temporary ingress rate-limit for new sessions. I'll run the toggle.
tess (eng-runtime): config to apply (kubectl patch snippet):
```
kubectl -n inference patch configmap cb-runtime-config --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/prefetch.max_concurrency","value":"16"}, {"op":"replace","path":"/data/microbatch.min_size","value":"8"}]'
```
sam (oncall): running patch now.
incident-bot: Deployment rollout started for configmap cb-runtime-config.
liam (sre): after patch, seeing microbatch size climb to 6-10 for a lot of traffic -> initial p95 drop to ~1.1s within 90s. queue depth dropping.
tess (eng-runtime): rolling out prefetch_throttle flag to remaining canary nodes. watch kv_cache_evictions metric.
liam (sre): kv.evictions rate fell 78% in region, prefetch misses also down.
nina (prod-ops): customer impact update: p95>2s now down to 0.15% overall, the two flagged customers moved back to normal but still under monitoring.
alina (support): notified customers with follow-up and timeline of mitigation applied.
sam (oncall): good. now double-check fallback policy — ensure any request failing to form batch gets handled via sync fallback to avoid timeouts. tess can you confirm fallback is enabled?
tess (eng-runtime): fallback mode was set to 'degrade-to-sync' by default, I confirmed it's active. pushing a minor tweak to reduce sync timeout from 5s -> 3s to avoid long waits.
sam (oncall): applied tweak.
incident-bot: Config update recorded, incident-major: continuous-batch-perf-high-latency mitigated (status: partial).
liam (sre): we should still schedule a short blameless postmortem: root cause likely prefetch thrash + high concurrency traffic pattern producing microbatch starvation and kv-cache regen. Might need more heuristics to limit prefetch on noisy tenants.
tess (eng-runtime): Agree. Temporary fix good, next steps: (a) add adaptive prefetch backoff when evictions spike, (b) add batcher smoothing so microbatch target doesn't oscillate, (c) add metric alert for microbatch_size variance > 40% over 1m.
nina (prod-ops): i'll coordinate customer comms summary and timeline.
sam (oncall): handing off to tess (oncall-next) for monitoring and postmortem followups. I'm going offline in 20m.
tess (eng-runtime): taking handoff. will keep monitoring for 2 hours, then create the incident ticket with timeline + logs + config diff.
liam (sre): logging final observations: peak queue_depth 740, peak inflight 512, peak kv_evictions/s 1200 -> after fix evictions/s ~260. saving graphs to incident board.
nina (prod-ops): closing loop: customer impact small but visible for a subset; recommended to proactively reach out to top 20 high-concurrency customers with mitigation notes.
alina (support): received. will draft the outreach.
sam (oncall): thanks team. reaction summary: :thumbsup: :wrench: will follow up in postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-1183. Assigned: tess (eng-runtime). Link: https://redwood.example/incidents/INC-2026-1183
